concepts.def: LIFO structure with push/pop; used in call stacks, expression evaluation, undo features.
FIFO structure with enqueue/dequeue; used in scheduling, breadth-first search, print spoolers.
Sequence of nodes with data and pointer to next; dynamic size; O(n) access.
Hierarchical structure with up to two children per node; balanced trees give O(log n) operations.
Key-value store using hash function; average O(1) lookup; collisions handled by chaining or open addressing.
Vertices and edges; directed/undirected, weighted; algorithms include Dijkstra (1959) shortest path.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Abstract Data Structures brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.
